title: Add up 13 numbers in how many reads?
hook: Running totals are quick to read but slow to change. One bit trick makes both quick.

doesNotKnow: that x & -x gives a hop that makes prefix sums and updates both take about log n cells

misconception: A running prefix-sum table is cheap to read, so changing one value only needs one cell touched.
objective: The learner can explain that a Fenwick cell i covers the last (i & -i) numbers up to i, so a prefix sum hops down by the lowest 1 bit (13 -> 12 -> 8: 3 reads for 13 numbers) and an update hops up by it (1, 2, 4, 8, 16: 5 cells), both about log2 n.

claims.text: Cell i of a Fenwick tree holds the sum of the last (i & -i) numbers up to position i, that is positions i - (i & -i) + 1 to i; i & -i is the lowest 1 bit of i.
claims.source: Fenwick (1994), 'A new data structure for cumulative frequency tables', Software: Practice and Experience 24(3) (citation from the brief: check before verifying). i & -i isolates the lowest set bit in two's complement (derivation: -i = ~i + 1). · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: VERIFIED: Demo CELL[i] = sum V[i-low(i)+1..i] with low(i) = i & -i; -i = ~i + 1 isolates the lowest set bit. Fenwick 1994, Softw. Pract. Exp. 24(3):327-336 (DOI 10.1002/spe.4380240306) confirmed bibliographically by web search; paper not opened (host blocked). Definition verified against the code and derivation. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): reveal sentence now reads 'An index's lowest 1 bit is its cell's range length'; reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. v4 reveal 'An index's lowest 1 bit is its cell's range length' and the stage note 'Cell i covers the last (i & −i) numbers up to i' match CELL[i] = sum V[i-low(i)+1..i]. Own node: i & -i equals the isolated lowest set bit for i = 1..64. Openable independent source: npm fenwick-tree@0.0.0 (tarball sha256 0e1184a1…dac9, 0-based variant where cell at covers (at & (at+1))..at, i.e. i-lowbit(i)+1..i for i = at+1) builds the same 16 cells 3 4 4 9 5 14 2 31 5 8 5 21 9 16 9 80 from the stage numbers and gives prefix 13 = 61. Fenwick 1994 not opened (hosts blocked).

Own node hopsDown(13) = 13, 12, 8 (1101, 1100, 1000); ranges 13, 9-12, 1-8 tile 1-13; sum 61 = RUN[13]. Prefix 15: 15, 14, 12, 8; prefix 7: 7, 6, 4. Reveal requires milestone tiled (start 13), so qSum exists. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): reveal wording now '...tile 1–13 with no gaps: 3 reads for 13 numbers (61)'; the read trail is drawn inside the picture; reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. claims.text: Changing position 1 hops up 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 16: 5 Fenwick cells change, while a plain running-total row changes all 16 entries (reveal: '5 cells changed, against all 16 in the Σ row'; picture: 'Fenwick cells changed: 5', 'Σ: plain running totals · changed: 16').
claims.source: Demo.tsx hopsUp(1); builder re-ran in Node: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]. Running-total row: every prefix total 1..16 includes position 1 (derivation). v2 draws both on stage after 'Change position 1' (milestone update). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node hopsUp(1) = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (5 cells); every running total 1..16 includes position 1, so all 16 change. Stage readouts 5 and 16 match. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): reveal wording and the counts' place changed (readouts folded into the picture); reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node hopsUp(1) = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (5); independently, position 1 lies in cell j iff j - lowbit(j) < 1, i.e. j is a power of two: {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}. Every running total 1..16 includes position 1, so all 16 change. Picture reads 'Fenwick cells changed: 5' and 'Σ: plain running totals · changed: 16'; reveal '5 cells changed, against all 16 in the Σ row'. claims.text: Both ways take about log2 n hops, not n.
claims.source: Down: i - lowbit(i) removes exactly one set bit, so at most popcount(i) <= floor(log2 n) + 1 hops. Up: i + lowbit(i) has a strictly higher lowest set bit, so at most floor(log2 n) + 1 hops within n. Here n = 16: at most 5 hops (the update from 1 takes exactly 5). Derivation; Fenwick (1994) cited from the brief, not opened, and the sentence does not depend on it. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Re-derived: down hops = popcount(i), up hops <= floor(log2 n) + 1. Own node over i = 1..16: max 4 down, max 5 up (from 1). 'About log2 n' accurate. Fenwick 1994 not opened; not needed. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): reveal wording; reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Re-derived: a down hop clears one set bit (at most floor(log2 n) + 1 hops), an up hop strictly raises the lowest set bit (at most floor(log2 n) + 1 within n). Own node over i = 1..16: max 4 down, max 5 up. 'About log2 n' accurate; does not rest on Fenwick 1994.

claims.text: Picture lines after 'Change position 1': 'Change position 1: hop up by adding the lowest 1 bit' / '1=00001 → 2=00010 → 4=00100 → 8=01000 → 16=10000'.
claims.source: Standard Fenwick update rule i += i & -i (Fenwick 1994, 'A new data structure for cumulative frequency tables'); the line is computed by hopsUp(1) and bin5 in Demo.tsx. Added v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave G) for the r7 finding that the up hop was not shown in binary. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: i += i & -i from 1 gives 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (each step doubles, since a power of two is its own lowest bit); independently, position 1 lies in cell j = (j - lowbit(j), j] only when j is a power of two, so for N = 16 the cells are exactly 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (Fenwick 1994 not opened; not needed). Generated line: "Change position 1, hop up by adding the lowest 1 bit: 1=00001 → 2=00010 → 4=00100 → 8=01000 → 16=10000". up is never cleared (button disabled once set), so the line stays. | v4 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14, wave H r8 phone fit): stage line reworded and moved into the picture; reopened, unverified. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: i += i & -i from 1 gives 1, 2, 4, 8, 16; bin5 gives 00001, 00010, 00100, 01000, 10000. Picture lines (y = BASE+92, BASE+106) read 'Change position 1: hop up by adding the lowest 1 bit' / '1=00001 → 2=00010 → 4=00100 → 8=01000 → 16=10000' once up is set; up never clears.

recall.question: In a Fenwick tree, the prefix sum up to position 22 (binary 10110) reads how many cells?
recall.why: One cell per 1 bit: 22 -> 20 -> 16 -> 0, reading cells 22, 20 and 16.
